DI G BACONC PILIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OILG OPINION NO. S. 2025 SEP 162025 ERWIN MALLANAO Blk I Lot I Circumferential Road Antipolo, Rizal erwinmallanao@gmail.com Dear Mr. Mallanao: This refers to your email addressed to the Presidential Action Center, Office of the President, dated May 8, 2025, which was endorsed to this Department. The said communication seeks clarification on whether a government employee, specifically a Municipal Engineer, may engage in private contracting projects while in government service. At the outset, please be informed that all government employees, including personnel of local government units such as municipal engineers, are subject to the jurisdiction of the Civil Service Commission (CSC), which is the central personnel agency of the government mandated to administer and enforce rules, policies, and regulations governing the civil service. Nonetheless, for purposes of general guidance and without prejudice to any definitive ruling by the CSC, we respectfully offer the following observations. Foremost, we invite your attention to Section 7 (b) (2) of Republic Act No. 67131 in relation to Section 11 of the same law, provides: "Section 7. Prohibited Acts and Transactions. — In addition to acts and omissions of public officials and employees now prescribed in the Constitution and existing laws, the following shall constitute prohibited acts and transactions of any public official and employee and are hereby declared to be unlawful: xxx xxx xxx b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto. — Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: I) Own, control, manage or accept employment as officer, employee, consultant, counsel, broker, agent, trustee or nominee in any private enterprise regulated, supervised or licensed by their office unless expressly allowed by law; Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

2) Engage in the private practice of their profession unless authorized by the Constitution or law, provided, that such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict with their official functions; or 3) Recommend any person to any position in a private enterprise which has a regular or pending official transaction with their office. These prohibitions shall continue to apply for a period of one (1) year after resignation, retirement, or separation from public office, except in the case of subparagraph (b) (2) above, but the professional concerned cannot practice his profession in connection with any matter before the office he used to be with, in which case the one-year prohibition shall likewise apply. Section 11. Penalties. — x x x Violations of Sections 7, 8 or 9 of this Act shall be punishable with imprisonment not exceeding five (5) years, ora fine not exceeding five (Php 5,000) or both x x x. Relative thereto, Section 136 of the 2017 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Actions states that. "Section 136. No officer or employee, whether in a permanent or regular capacity, temporary, casual, or hold-over, shall engage directly or indirectly in any private business or practice of profession. Exemptions may be allowed, subject to the limitations provided under RA No. 6713 and other special laws. Provided, further that the following requirements/conditions are met: a. Written permission from head of agency must be secured and renewed annually; b. Time devoted outside of office hours shall not impair in any way the efficiency of the officer or employee nor pose a conflict or tend to conflict with the official functions and must be fixed by the head of agency; and c. Government facilities, equipment and supplies shall not be used while engaged in private business or practice of profession" Clearly, public officials and employees are prohibited from engaging in the private practice of their profession during their incumbency, unless expressly authorized by law or the Constitution, and provided that such practice does not conflict with their official duties and responsibilities. Accordingly, a municipal engineer is legally restricted from rendering professional services for private contracting projects or similar engagements, as his primary obligation is to devote full time and attention to public service However, an exception is recognized when there is a written authorization from the head of the agency concerned—specifically, the local chief executive (i.e., the Mayor)—allowing such official to engage in the private practice of his profession. Even then, this written permission is not absolute. It is subject to the condition that the private engagement must not impair the efficiency of the official concerned nor give rise to a conflict of interest. Page 2 of 3

In this regard, it must be emphasized that the authorized private practice must not conflict with the interest of the local govemment unit (LGU) or be inconsistent with the duties and responsibilities of the official in said LGU_ Any private contract or undertaking that may compromise the impartiality, integrity, or effectiveness of the municipal engineer's public office is strictly prohibited. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY. OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLNRPB/LLLS-LLRALDtmag/kbm Page 3 of 3
